card.hook: Imagine a stone wall zigzagging up a mountain like it's late for something, all the way to a castle at about 280 m. That's Kotor's skyline, and it looks best from across the water.
card.stand_here: Stand on the Muo waterfront, across the narrow inlet from the Old Town. It's about 1.4 km from the fortifications in a straight line. Face south-east towards the walls and the mountain, and stand at the waterfront edge so the water fills the bottom of your frame.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x to catch the water, the Old Town and the wall climbing the hill. Then try zoom 2x-5x (higher zooms depend on your phone) to pick out the zigzag and the castle on the ridge. Use zoom 0.5x only if you want lots of waterfront, because it makes the walls look small and far away.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines and put the waterline on the lower grid line so the horizon stays level, with the top third left for the wall and the mountain.
card.best_time: Go for sunset, when the stone turns gold. Be in place a little beforehand and take several shots as the light changes. After sunset, switch to night mode and hold your phone very still.
card.selfie_here: Try the bank across the moat from the Kotor City Walls. Sit down, use the front camera, and look up so the walls fill the frame behind you with the water in front. At the entrance to St John's Fortress, golden hour lights the stone walls nicely behind you.
card.ask_someone: On the bridge near Kampana Tower, ask a passer-by to try a few spots along the bridge until the round tower and the walls climbing the hill both fit in the frame with you.
card.rules_and_safety: Walking the city walls in summer? Avoid the heat of the day and bring plenty of water. The Muo waterfront is a public street, but climbing the fortress itself may be ticketed or restricted, so check the official site first.
card.challenge: Catch a boat gliding through the bottom of your frame while the wall glows gold above it. Try a Live Photo and pick your favourite moment.
card.good_to_know: The outer wall is about 4.5 km round, 2 to 16 m thick and up to 20 m high. The hill was fortified in Illyrian times, and the Byzantines, Venetians and Austrians all added to it. Most of what you see was built by the Venetians, who took over in 1420, and the walls and Old Town have been a World Heritage Site since 1979.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand on the Muo waterfront, across the narrow inlet from the Old Town. It's about 1.4 km from the fortifications in a straight line. Face south-east towards the walls and the mountain, and stand at the waterfront edge so the water fills the bottom of your frame.

card.hook: Ever tried to fit a 12th-century cathedral into a phone screen? You'll be craning your neck, because Kotor Cathedral is big, pale and very close.
card.stand_here: Stand at Pjaca Svetog Tripuna, about 30 m west of the cathedral, and face east. You're close, so the building will fill much of your screen.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 0.5x to squeeze the whole front in, then go to 1x for a more natural look. If your phone has 2x or 5x, use them to pick out the carvings higher up.
card.make_it_pop: Switch on gridlines and line the building's edges up with the vertical lines so the walls stand straight instead of leaning.
card.best_time: Early morning or late afternoon usually means softer light and fewer people in your shot.
card.selfie_here: Head to the small well in the middle of the square and stand with the cathedral facade behind you. Use the front camera at 0.5x so the whole facade fits over your shoulder.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand at the fountain and back up until the whole facade fits, while you stand in front of the cathedral. For a nicer angle on the towers, they can stand on the left side of the square, looking right.
card.rules_and_safety: The cathedral is a working place of worship, so check the official site before you go for visiting arrangements and whether photography is allowed inside.
card.challenge: Take one shot of the whole front, then walk closer and snap the stonework texture. Bonus points if you can't tell which one is the same building.
card.good_to_know: The cathedral is dedicated to Saint Tryphon, Kotor's patron, who also appears on the city's coat of arms. It was consecrated on 19 June 1166 on the site of an older church from 809. It was badly damaged in the 1667 and 1979 earthquakes, and a long renovation was celebrated with a blessing in December 2000.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand at Pjaca Svetog Tripuna, about 30 m west of the cathedral, and face east. You're close, so the building will fill much of your screen.

card.hook: Somewhere around step 400 your legs will start filing complaints, and then this little pale church turns up against the whole bay like it's been waiting for you. It's one of those spots where the view does the hard work.
card.stand_here: Stand at the Church of Our Lady of Remedy, a little higher on the fortress path above the church, and face down and out. The church should sit in front of the bay, the Old Town walls and the Vrmac ridge.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x to get the church with the bay and ridge behind it. Switch to zoom 0.5x to fit in more of the Old Town walls and the whole sweep of the bay. Try zoom 2x or higher (depends on your phone) to pick out just the church.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on the gridlines and put the church on one of the lower lines, so the bay and the ridge fill the top of the picture.
card.best_time: Early morning or late afternoon is worth trying for softer light than the middle of the day. We don't have exact timings for this one, so check how the light looks when you get there.
card.selfie_here: Head to the terrace of the Church of Our Lady of Remedy and face out over the bay with the church behind you. Use the front camera at zoom 0.5x so the church fits over your shoulder with the water beside you.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand on the path at the first bend above the church and shoot down toward you at the church, with the Old Town and bay behind.
card.rules_and_safety: The stone steps are worn smooth and can be very slippery, especially on the way down, so wear sturdy shoes. Fees and opening times can change, so check the official site before you go.
card.challenge: Get the church, the water and the ridge all in one frame, and bonus points if you can still smile after 650 steps.
card.good_to_know: The church was finished in 1518 and is also called Gospa od Zdravlja, or Our Lady of Health. You can only get there on foot, up a stairway of more than 650 steps. Under it, an early Christian basilica from the 6th century has been found, the oldest known building in Montenegro.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand at the Church of Our Lady of Remedy, a little higher on the fortress path above the church, and face down and out. The church should sit in front of the bay, the Old Town walls and the Vrmac ridge.

selfie_spots.why: A travel guide says the views from the church terrace are already superb, so standing there with the bay in front and the church at your back should give a good selfie.

selfie_research.safety: The stone steps are worn smooth and can be very slippery, especially on the way down, so sturdy footwear is needed.
selfie_research.notes: No page I found states rules on selfie sticks or tripods. The selfie spot is a judgement from a terrace description, not a page that names a selfie position with the church directly behind. The ask-someone spot comes from a page describing a photo taken from the bend with the church in view, not a photo of a visitor. Sources disagree on the step count to the church (about 650 on Wikipedia and Adriatic Ways, versus about 1,350 for the full fortress route). Sources also disagree on whether there is a fee: one review says 15 euros, another says there is no fee to enter the church, and one review says the church was closed. Check locally before going.

card.hook: Picture a stone arch, a wall of mountains right behind it, and a row of boat masts poking up along the bottom of your screen. That's the Sea Gate, and it's the shot everyone comes to Kotor for.
card.stand_here: Stand on Riva (middle of the waterfront promenade, roughly opposite the Sea Gate, shooting slightly north). Face the gate so you get the arch and the base of the Old Town walls with the mountains behind.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x for the classic view. If you're close and the walls get cut off, tap 0.5x. If your phone has zoom 2x, use it to pick out the carved lion above the arch.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines to keep the walls straight, then tap the stone of the gate and drag the slider a little darker so the bright sky doesn't wash out the detail.
card.best_time: Go early, ideally before about 9:00 in summer. The light falls on the lion of St Mark above the arch and the entrance is at its quietest. Later in the day cruise passengers crowd in.
card.selfie_here: Head to the oversized bench just outside the Sea Gate entrance, on the outer side of the gate. It's a fun prop, so use the front camera, try 0.5x and keep the gate behind your shoulder.
card.ask_someone: Stand in front of the gate and ask a passer-by to stand on the waterfront promenade with the gate straight ahead of them, ideally before 9:00 in the morning.
card.challenge: Find the lion of St Mark above the arch, zoom in on it, then try to get a frame where the masts lead your eye straight to the gate.
card.good_to_know: The Sea Gate is a busy waterfront entrance to Kotor's Old Town, facing the Riva promenade. Above the arch is a carved lion of St Mark. For a second shot, walk through and look back from inside, where the arch frames the bright bay.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand on Riva (middle of the waterfront promenade, roughly opposite the Sea Gate, shooting slightly north). Face the gate so you get the arch and the base of the Old Town walls with the mountains behind.
